title: Take-Two CEO：Grand Theft Auto VI 预购量超出预期

Grand Theft Auto VI beats Take-Two's pre-order expectations
Business
Console
PC
News
Take-Two CEO: Grand Theft Auto VI pre-orders are exceeding expectations
It's not entirely clear what those expectations were, but Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss Zelnick is boasting about the game's sales on the eve of its long-anticipated release.
Imran Khan
,
Contributing Editor
,
GameDeveloper.com
November 10, 2026
schedule
2 Min Read
via Rockstar
Take-Two has reported its fiscal quarter earnings for the quarter preceding
Grand Theft Auto VI
's arrival, reporting slight downturns in net bookings and revenue year-over-year, with its Q2 net bookings figure falling slightly below its forecasts but GAAP net revenue falling within expectations.
While the game industry is collectively holding its breath for
Grand Theft Auto VI's
upcoming launch, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick claimed that preorders for one of the most anticipated media releases of all time are exceeding the company's expectations. In a comment made during
the second quarter earnings briefing
, Zelnick commented that—despite
GTA 6
not officially being released for another week—its launch trajectory is "tracking far above our initial expectations" in terms of preorder volume.
Zelnick did not expound further on Take-Two's preorder expectations for the sequel, which itself is the followup to one of the best-selling video games in history. Some analysts believe the game
will sell more than 50 million copies in its first year
, which may mean that even potentially lofty expectations could be exceeded. On the other hand, it is difficult to say how conservative Take-Two's launch projections might be without direct numbers.

Backing up the publisher's optimism is confirmation from PlayStation that Grand Theft Auto VI is officially
the most pre-ordered game in the history of the PlayStation store
, presumably since the store opened in 2006, but likewise did not share direct numbers.
The Silence Before the Storm
In other Take-Two financial news,
GTA 6's
predecessor,
Grand Theft Auto V
, reached 235 million copies sold in the last quarter, pushing the overall franchise numbers for the entire Grand Theft Auto series to 480 million units.
Net bookings and net revenue for the company are down overall for the quarter ending September 30, 2026 when compared to the year prior, largely owed to a slow start for
NBA 2K27
, which Zelnick explains away
in an interview with IGN
as suffering from proximity to
Grand Theft Auto VI
. This year, Take-Two reported $1.6 billion in net bookings, down $276.8 million and 1.2 percent shy of targets, while net revenue came in at $1.497 billion, down $276.8 million and slightly above forecasts. For the same period, operating profit decreased by roughly $19.5 million, going from last year's loss of $98 million to a loss of $117.5 million this quarter.
Upcoming guidance, though, expects net bookings to exceed $8 billion for the full fiscal year, likely with
GTA 6
leading the charge.

Report: Silver Lake and the Saudi Arabia PIF hold talks with Unity to explore acquisition
This reporting focused largely on
Grand Theft Auto VI
for good reason, and its a pattern that's reflected in Take-Two's current public product pipeline as well. While the company has announced that upcoming titles like a new
Bioshock
game and Ken Levine's
Judas
are in development, nothing on the publisher's release schedule has a date beyond
Grand Theft Auto VI
. For better or worse, the future is shaped like Vice City.
